subject: Cessna 172 airplane
title: The 5 Most-Built Airplanes Ever, Ranked (#1 Never Fired a Shot)

scenes.text: The five most-built airplanes ever. Number one never fired a shot, and you can still buy one.
Number five: the Cessna one-fifty and one-fifty-two. About thirty-one thousand built, with just two seats.
scenes.label: Cessna 150/152 · 31,000

scenes.text: Number four: the Piper Cherokee. Over thirty-two thousand, and Piper has built it since 1960.
scenes.label: Piper Cherokee · 32,000

scenes.text: Number three: the Messerschmitt one-oh-nine. About thirty-five thousand, Germany's main fighter of World War Two.
scenes.label: Messerschmitt Bf 109 · 35,000

scenes.text: Number two: the Ilyushin Il-2. Over thirty-six thousand of these armored Soviet attack planes.
scenes.label: Ilyushin Il-2 · 36,000

scenes.text: Number one: the Cessna one-seventy-two. More than forty-four thousand since 1955, and still coming off the line. It's probably parked at your local airfield.
scenes.label: Cessna 172 · 44,000+

description:
The five most-produced airplanes in history, ranked by total number built.
The Cessna 150 and 152 two-seat trainers reached about 31,000; Piper's PA-28 Cherokee family passed 32,000 and is still in production; about 35,000 Messerschmitt Bf 109 fighters were built in World War II; the armored Ilyushin Il-2 attack plane reached about 36,000; and the Cessna 172 Skyhawk, first flown in 1955, has passed 44,000 and is still being built.
Which plane did you expect at number one?
first_comment: Which would you put at number one? The Soviet Po-2 biplane may belong on this list too, but estimates run from 20,000 to 40,000, so nobody knows. What should we rank next?
